ask.text: Maria asks in her own words.
Our model writes the definition of done, with a typical price range.

find.text: Her agent finds the pros nearby and reads their reviews.
The agents bargain in rounds, and VeriPay shows where each price sits in the market, and warns her when a deal isn't coming together.

offers.text: Eastside's agent comes down to $185, and hers hires inside a signed mandate capped at $200.
A lower cap, or a replay, is refused.

chat.text: from a chat, she can post a job, compare offers and bargain.
Hiring still comes back to VeriPay, and her PIN.

hold.text: On site, a $47.05 valve is over her agent's limit, so only Maria's PIN can approve it, and PayPal re-holds $247.05 on her saved card.

phone.text: The plumber sends photos and the receipt from his phone.

checks.text: Our models read the photos and the receipt;
code checks when and where each was taken.
A note hiding an instruction is flagged, and the money waits for a person.

paid.text: code captures exactly $232.05, one Payouts batch pays the pro, and an agent reconciles both with PayPal.

arch.text: Any agent can drive it, over MCP, A2A or REST.
But every money move passes one guard in our code:
The money itself runs on PayPal.

hood.text: Under the hood it's all PayPal:
Orders authorizes, the Vault re-holds, a partial capture takes what's due, Payouts pays the pro, and the Agent Toolkit reconciles.

scale.text: It scales to materials, Pay Later, landlords and neighbors, with an AG Grid back office.
AI agents tested it in forty-five runs over eleven rounds;

vision.text: Log in with PayPal, live payouts to every pro, and any job a photo can prove.

end.text: The money waits for the proof.

pain1.text: Maria paid the plumber up front.
He took the cash, and her faucet still drips.

pain2.text: The client said "later," and he's still waiting to get paid.

solution.text: PayPal holds the money without charging it, AI checks the work, and the pro is paid the moment it passes.
Built for homeowners and the small pros they hire.

impact.text: Home repair is a $525 billion a year market, where four in five trade businesses are one-person shops, and PayPal already has 440 million accounts on both sides.

novel.text: What we did not find anywhere else in agentic commerce:
an open agent-to-agent platform for local work.
Agents do it all by default, bargain in rounds, and AI checks every payment step, while only code moves the money.

models.text: We fine-tuned 0.6-billion-parameter models from a 30-billion open teacher.
On held-out tests, the audit model gets 99.9% of verdicts right, and it runs on one GPU in about a third of a second.

features.text: In all, we tracked 219 PayPal features:
188 are built, and 91 are verified in the real sandbox.

product.text: 28 pages for five roles, from the customer's agent and the pro's phone, in English or Spanish, to landlords, inspectors and the back office.
